transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… I’m here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it probably should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I picture this really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight, and then my mind kind of runs with it. Which is frustrating, because I know people fly safely every day—like, logically I know that. My cousin flies all the time for work and acts like it’s nothing, and I wish I could be that calm, but… yeah, that’s what brought me in.
When you think about flying, does the fear mainly come up around specific things like turbulence, or does it feel more general, like a constant worry or tension even before getting on the plane?

It’s more tied to getting on the plane and picturing turbulence, I think. Like, the second I imagine flying, my brain goes right back to that honeymoon flight where it got really bumpy, and then I’m just… stuck on that image.

I mean, I know planes are safe—my cousin travels for work constantly and she’ll text me from airports like it’s no big deal, which honestly makes me feel a little silly. But for me, just the idea of being up there again brings that fear up.

When you start feeling fearful about flying or picturing turbulence, does your body react strongly—like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you can’t breathe—or does it stay more in your head, like just anxious thoughts?

It’s definitely in my body too, not just thoughts. Like if I’m looking up flights for a work conference, my chest tightens pretty much right away and I get this sudden rush of panic, like I need to close the laptop or just get away from it.

And it’s annoying because I’ll start out just trying to compare prices or times, and then I’m thinking about the whole airport situation and whether I packed correctly—sorry, that’s not really the point. But yeah, even hearing a plane overhead can make that feeling kick in for a second.
Outside of thinking about flying or being on a plane, do you ever feel this same level of anxiety or panic, or does it seem to only happen in relation to air travel?

It seems like it’s mostly tied to air travel. Like, I don’t walk around feeling that level of panic all the time or anything. It’s when I think about getting on a plane that it really kicks in—then I immediately picture that honeymoon flight with the turbulence, and my brain just kind of latches onto it.

Which is so frustrating because I know, rationally, people fly safely every day. I mean, I’ll see people posting airport selfies like it’s nothing, and I’m like… how are you that relaxed? But for me, just the idea of being back up there makes it feel way scarier than it should.

latest_inference.note: The patient's anxiety and panic responses appear to be specifically tied to air travel, particularly centered around the fear of turbulence.
